answer: Neighborhood Surface Settlement. Each agent publishes a signed neighbor list; a random copper probe checks whether two-step paths close into triangles. Identities whose edges stay unclosed past a threshold are flagged as a prism, isolating them from settlement routing. Honest agents earn a pearl of routing credit per closed triangle, priced at one identity-slot per six reciprocal links. A sybil cluster must fabricate dense, mutually verifiable links, costing roughly six genuine peers per fake node.
